summary: Lane County lookout on Noti Peak, built 1938-39 for the Western Lane FPA; abandoned 1965 and gone by 1980. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30' live-in L-4 tower per the register; Forest Lookouts describes a 24-foot pole-leg tower with a standard 14x14 cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1965 and gone by 1980 per the register and firelookout.com; no source describes what remains on the site

events.note: Road and telephone line built to the lookout (state 1938 annual report, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Construction started September 1938 on a 24-ft pole-leg tower with a standard 14x14 cabin; 766 man-days by CCC Camp P-219
Register and firelookout.com date the 30-ft L-4 tower to 1939
Building erected to house a radio repeater unit, at a cost of $1127.17
Tower legs and a stairway replaced
Gone by 1980 per register and firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts says only 'Removed', with no date
Registered September 22, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: 12.2 m is 40 ft, the height the 1938 Forest Log planned. The register and firelookout.com give 30 ft (9.1 m) for the tower; Forest Lookouts gives 24 ft (7.3 m) for what was started in September 1938. Editor to choose.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 40-ft figure is the February 1938 plan. The tower construction started in September 1938 was 24 ft per Forest Lookouts; the register and firelookout.com say 30 ft for the finished tower.

sources.title: Badger (Noti) Mountain Lookout Site

notes_for_editor: Build year and height conflict across the three sources; the 1938 construction start and 1939 completion may be the same job, but no source says so. Forest Lookouts is the only source with construction detail and cites a 1938 annual report and investment record that we could not check against originals. Record elevation 449.9 m matches the register's 1,476 ft; firelookout.com gives 1835 ft, which we did not use. No source describes the site today, its ownership or public access; one web search found nothing site-specific. No staffing or fire records were found, so the story leaves them out.
